history.heading: Great empires
paragraphs: Mali was the heart of some of West Africa's greatest empires. The Ghana Empire extended into its territory. The Mali Empire, founded by Sundiata Keita around 1235, became one of the largest and richest states in the world; Mansa Musa's lavish pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 made Mali famous for its gold.

The Songhai Empire, centred on Gao, succeeded Mali in the 15th century. Timbuktu became a centre of Islamic scholarship, with libraries of manuscripts and the great mosques of Djinguereber and Sankore. Djenné's mud-brick Great Mosque is the largest earthen building in the world. A Moroccan invasion in 1591 ended Songhai power.

history.heading: French Sudan and independence
paragraphs: France conquered the region in the late 19th century, overcoming resistance by leaders such as Samori Touré and the Toucouleur Empire, and it became the colony of French Sudan. Mali became independent on 22 September 1960 under Modibo Keïta, who pursued socialist policies.
Moussa Traoré seized power in 1968 and ruled until a popular uprising and coup in 1991. Mali then became a democracy, with Alpha Oumar Konaré as president from 1992.

history.heading: Crisis since 2012
paragraphs: In 2012 Tuareg separatists and jihadist groups seized northern Mali, destroying ancient shrines in Timbuktu. French intervention in 2013 drove them out of the towns, but insurgency spread to central Mali, with thousands killed.

Military coups occurred in 2020 and 2021, bringing Colonel Assimi Goïta to power. The junta expelled French troops and the UN mission, turned to Russian forces, and with Burkina Faso and Niger formed the Alliance of Sahel States and left ECOWAS. In 2025 jihadists imposed a fuel blockade on Bamako.

culture.heading: Music and heritage
paragraphs: Mali's music is world famous: Ali Farka Touré, Toumani Diabaté (kora), Salif Keita, Oumou Sangaré, Amadou & Mariam and the Tuareg band Tinariwen. Griots preserve oral history through song, including the Epic of Sundiata.

The main groups include the Bambara, Fula, Soninke, Songhai, Tuareg and Dogon, whose cliff villages are a UNESCO site. Bambara is widely spoken, and about 95 percent of people are Muslim. Bogolanfini (mud cloth) is a distinctive textile.

politics.heading: Military rule
paragraphs: Mali is ruled by a military junta. A 2023 constitution strengthened presidential powers, and in 2025 political parties were dissolved and Goïta was granted a renewable five-year presidential term without election. The government faces a serious insurgency by groups linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

economy.heading: Gold and cotton
paragraphs: Mali is one of Africa's largest gold producers, and gold dominates exports, followed by cotton. Most people depend on farming, herding and fishing along the Niger River. The junta has sought a greater share of mining revenues, leading to disputes with foreign companies.
Mali is among the poorest countries in the world, and conflict has displaced hundreds of thousands. The currency is the West African CFA franc.
